text: Two confirmed findings, two fixes. The autoscaling fix is a one-line Terraform change: the module now references the standard profile instead of peak-season, going through a pull request and terraform plan like any other production change.

Validation means two kinds of evidence. kubectl get hpa confirms the cluster is actually running two replicas, not ten. A few days later, Azure Cost Analysis confirms the forecast has settled back toward the original seventeen-fifty projection.
The bucket policy fix replaces the wildcard Principal with the specific ARN of the driftwood-backup-writer role, and turns on S3 Block Public Access across all four settings.

Validation again means two checks: aws s3api get-bucket-policy-status confirms IsPublic is now false, and the cross-cloud replication job from Lesson Seven still runs successfully end to end, proving the fix didn't lock out the one principal that's supposed to have access.

Neither fix was a late-night emergency patch. Both went through review and came with concrete after-the-fact evidence, not just an assumption the change worked. Next lesson turns that discipline into something automatic.
